title: “We will keep enforcing our artists’ rights... but it’s becoming an uphill struggle”: Sony Music reveals the number of deepfake AI tracks it’s asked to be removed has doubled in six months
key_facts: Sony Music says takedown requests for AI deepfake tracks have doubled in six months.
MusicRadar says Sony asked streamers to remove 260,000 tracks in the year to September, against 135,000 in the year to March.
Sony says the problem of deepfakes imitating artists' voices without permission is 'happening at scale'.
Sony says: 'it's becoming an uphill struggle'.
In May, Sony's Dennis Kooker said between 5% and 10% of streams could be fraudulent, which he called possible.
MusicRadar says the figure is probably a fraction of what gets through.
quote_evidence: We will keep enforcing our artists’ rights and expect platforms to act quickly and to prevent the same content from reappearing. But it’s becoming an uphill struggle.

Sony has said that the problem of “generative AI deepfake tracks that imitate our artists’ voices and likenesses without permission” was “happening at scale, harms artists, misleads fans and undermines the ethical use of AI”.
why_it_matters_hint: Sony's numbers show deepfake music is growing faster than takedowns can keep up.
notes: The two periods in the article are not identical (year to September vs year to March); kept as MusicRadar states them.
